# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p meshmind-mcp --example tool_docs > docs/TOOLS.md`. Do not edit by hand. -->

These are the tools MeshMind gives your AI agent. You normally don't call them yourself; the agent reads these descriptions and picks the right ones.

## `create_primitive`

Add a new object from a basic shape, centred on the origin (Y is up, units are metres). Returns its id. Most models start from a few primitives that are then edited and combined.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | number | Cylinder and cone height. Default 1. |
| `name` | string | Display name, e.g. "Table leg". |
| `radius` | number | Sphere, cylinder and cone radius; torus ring radius. Default 0.5. |
| `rings` | integer | Sphere rings, or torus tube segments. Default 16. |
| `segments` | integer | Detail around the axis. Default 32. |
| `shape` (required) | one of `cube`, `plane`, `sphere`, `cylinder`, `cone`, `torus` |  |
| `size` | number | Cube/plane edge length. Default 1. |
| `tube_radius` | number | Torus tube radius. Default 0.15. |

## `loft`

Create an object by sweeping one cross-section shape up the Y axis through stations, each scaling and shifting it. The way to model blades, swords, knives, horns, tapered handles, table legs and spires. Example sword blade: a lens or diamond `shape` about 1 wide and 0.2 thick, stations [{y:0, scale:[0.025,0.03]}, {y:0.65, scale:[0.022,0.025]}, {y:0.78, scale:[0.012,0.02]}, {y:0.82, scale:[0,0]}] for a blade 5 cm wide tapering to a point. A concave shape (a groove in each face) makes a fuller. Edges sharper than 50 degrees render crisp, so a pointed shape gives a sharp cutting edge.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |
| `shape` (required) | array of array | Closed outline as [x, z] points (3 or more), centred on 0. Scaled by each station. |
| `stations` (required) | array of object | 2 or more cross-sections from bottom to top. |

## `lathe`

Create a round object by spinning a side profile around the Y axis, like a potter's wheel. The way to model pommels, knobs, bottles, vases, goblets, wheels, columns and finials. Profile points are [radius, y] from bottom to top; radius 0 closes the shape on the axis. Sharp corners in the profile stay crisp.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |
| `profile` (required) | array of array | [radius, y] points in metres, in order along the outline. |
| `segments` | integer | Detail around the axis. Default 32; use 6 or 8 for faceted shapes. |

## `extrude_outline`

Create a flat-sided object from a 2D outline (in the XY plane) with a thickness along Z. The way to model crossguards, axe heads, shields, brackets, signs, gears and any silhouette. Concave outlines are fine. Bevel it afterwards to soften the edges.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` (required) | number | Thickness along Z in metres, centred on z = 0. |
| `name` | string |  |
| `outline` (required) | array of array | Closed outline as [x, y] points in metres (3 or more). |

## `sweep`

Create a round tube along a path: rope, cables, pipes, rails, rings, chains, and leather or wire wrapped around a grip (use `helix`). Give either `path` points or `helix`.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `helix` | object | A spiral around Y centred on the origin, e.g. a grip wrap: {radius: 0.017, height: 0.14, turns: 10}. |
| `name` | string |  |
| `path` | array of array | [x, y, z] points in metres. Repeat the first point at the end for a closed loop. |
| `radii` | array of number | Optional radius per path point (tapering tubes). |
| `radius` (required) | number | Tube radius in metres. |
| `segments` | integer | Detail around the tube. Default 12. |

## `deform`

Bend, twist or taper a whole object along an axis (curved blades and horns, twisted bars and ropes, tapering legs and towers). The low end of the axis stays put. Edge loops are added automatically so the curve is smooth.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` (required) | number | taper: scale at the far end (0 = point, 0.5 = half). twist and bend: degrees. |
| `axis` | one of `x`, `y`, `z` | Along which local axis. Default y. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `loops` | integer | Edge loops to add first. Default 24 for bend and twist, 0 for taper. |
| `mode` (required) | one of `taper`, `twist`, `bend` |  |
| `toward` | one of `x`, `y`, `z` | bend: which axis the object curves towards (positive side; use a negative amount for the other way). Default x. |

## `slice`

Add evenly spaced edge loops across an object along an axis, so later edits (deform, move_vertices) have vertices to work with.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axis` (required) | one of `x`, `y`, `z` |  |
| `cuts` (required) | integer |  |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `move_vertices`

Move or scale the vertices of an object inside a world-space box, for shaping details: pinch a tip, flare a guard's ends, push a dent, widen one end. `falloff` blends the edit smoothly into the surrounding surface. Use slice first if the area has no vertices.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `falloff` | number | Width of the soft blend around the box in metres. Default 0. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `max` (required) | array of number | Opposite box corner. |
| `min` (required) | array of number | Box corner (world space, metres). |
| `scale` | array of number | Scale around the box centre, e.g. [1.5, 1, 1.5]. |
| `translate` | array of number | Move by [x, y, z] metres. |

## `list_objects`

List all objects with id, name, transform, world-space size and bounding box, face count and material.

## `get_object`

Details of one object, including each face's index, centre and normal (local space), so you can pick faces by index for extrude/inset.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `max_faces` | integer | Limit on faces listed. Default 100. |

## `set_transform`

Move, rotate or scale an object. Omitted fields keep their value. Rotation is Euler degrees applied X, then Y, then Z.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `rotation_degrees` | array of number | Rotation [x, y, z] in degrees. |
| `scale` | array of number | Scale [x, y, z]. |
| `translation` | array of number | Position [x, y, z]. |

## `duplicate_object`

Copy an object, including its transform and material. Returns the new id.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `delete_object`

Remove an object.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `clear_scene`

Remove every object. Can be undone.

## `extrude`

Push the selected faces out along their normals as one region, adding side walls. Negative distance pushes in, making a recess. Use for legs, handles, panels, greebles.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `distance` (required) | number | Metres. |
| `faces` (required) | any | Which faces to affect. "all"; or {"facing": "+y"} to pick faces pointing a world direction ("+x", "-x", "+y", "-y", "+z", "-z" or [x, y, z]), with optional "max_angle" in degrees (default 30); or a list of face indices from get_object. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `inset`

Shrink each selected face towards its centre, leaving a border ring. Returns inner_faces: extrude exactly those (pass the list as `faces`) by a small negative distance for recessed panels, or positive for raised ones. Selecting by direction again would also catch the ring.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` (required) | number | 0 to 1: fraction of the way to the centre. Typical 0.1 to 0.3. |
| `faces` (required) | any | Which faces to affect. "all"; or {"facing": "+y"} to pick faces pointing a world direction ("+x", "-x", "+y", "-y", "+z", "-z" or [x, y, z]), with optional "max_angle" in degrees (default 30); or a list of face indices from get_object. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `bevel`

Round off the hard edges of a closed object (edges where faces meet at more than `angle` degrees, default 30). Real objects never have perfectly sharp edges: a small rounded bevel (1 to 3% of the object's size) is one of the biggest steps towards a professional look. Curved surfaces like a cylinder's side are left alone. Use segments 1 for a flat chamfer (machined or cut look), 3 to 5 for rounded edges.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` (required) | number | Bevel width in metres. |
| `angle` | number | Only edges sharper than this many degrees. Default 30. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `segments` | integer | 1 = flat chamfer, more = rounder. Default 3. |

## `subdivide`

Split every face into smaller faces. smooth=true (default) rounds the shape (Catmull-Clark), good for organic forms and soft edges. Each level makes about 4x the faces.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `levels` | integer | Default 1. |
| `smooth` | boolean |  |

## `boolean`

Combine two objects. "difference" cuts the tool object out of the target (holes, notches), "union" merges them, "intersection" keeps the overlap. The result replaces the target; the tool object is deleted unless keep_tool is true. Both should be closed shapes.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `keep_tool` | boolean |  |
| `operation` (required) | one of `union`, `difference`, `intersection` |  |
| `target` (required) | integer |  |
| `tool` (required) | integer |  |

## `mirror`

Mirror an object across its local origin plane and join both halves. Faces lying on the mirror plane are removed, so model one half, then mirror for perfect symmetry.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axis` (required) | one of `x`, `y`, `z` |  |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `array`

Repeat an object's mesh several times inside the same object, each copy shifted by offset (metres). Good for rails, bolts, steps, fences.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `count` (required) | integer |  |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `offset` (required) | array of number | Shift between copies [x, y, z]. |

## `set_shading`

Smooth shading hides facets on curved surfaces; flat shading keeps hard edges.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `smooth` (required) | boolean |  |

## `set_material`

Create a PBR material and assign it to an object. Colors are linear RGB 0 to 1 (or use base_color_hex for an sRGB hex colour). Use metallic 1 for bare metals and 0 for everything else (paint, plastic, wood, stone). Roughness 0 is mirror-like, 1 is fully matte.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `base_color` | array of number |  |
| `base_color_hex` | string | Colour as sRGB hex, e.g. "#c0392b", instead of `base_color`. |
| `emissive` | array of number | Glow color, linear RGB. Values above 1 glow brighter. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `ior` | number | Index of refraction for transmissive materials: 1.33 water, 1.5 glass (default), 1.77 ruby, 2.42 diamond. |
| `metallic` | number |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `roughness` | number |  |
| `transmission` | number | 1 = clear like glass or water, tinted by base_color; 0 = opaque (default). Use roughness near 0 for clear glass, 0.3+ for frosted. |

## `unwrap_uvs`

Lay the object's surface flat into texture space (UV unwrapping). apply_smart_material does this automatically; call it yourself only to re-unwrap. Any geometry edit clears UVs.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |

## `apply_smart_material`

Give an object a realistic, textured material in one step: the surface is unwrapped and textures are generated from its shape. Paint chips off convex edges, dirt and rust collect in creases, colour varies naturally and fine bumps go into a normal map. This is the main way to get an AAA look; plain set_material looks like clean CG. Do it after the shape is final (geometry edits make the textures outdated). Bevel hard edges first: wear follows them.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | array of number | Main colour, linear RGB 0 to 1 (paint colour for painted_metal). Defaults to the preset's. |
| `color_hex` | string | Main colour as sRGB hex, e.g. "#5a6b2e", instead of `color`. |
| `dirt` | number | Grime in creases and dust: 0 clean, 1 filthy. Default 0.3. |
| `id` (required) | integer | Object id. |
| `preset` (required) | one of `painted_metal`, `bare_metal`, `rusty_metal`, `plastic`, `wood`, `stone`, `rubber`, `polished_metal`, `gold`, `leather`, `bronze`, `fabric`, `ceramic`, `bone`, `glass`, `gemstone` | painted_metal (paint over metal), bare_metal (cast or machined), rusty_metal, polished_metal (blades, armour, chrome: mirror-like, brushed along Y), gold (also brass via color), bronze (green verdigris patina in creases), leather (grips, straps, belts), fabric (woven cloth: banners, sacks, upholstery), ceramic (glazed pottery, tiles; chips show clay), bone (also ivory, horn), glass (clear and see-through; color tints it), gemstone (see-through, saturated: ruby by default), plastic, wood, stone (also concrete), rubber. |
| `resolution` | one of  | Texture size. Default 1024. |
| `scale` | number | Size of patterns (blotches, wood grain) in metres. Default 0.15. |
| `seed` | integer | Change for a different random pattern. |
| `wear` | number | Edge wear: 0 new, 0.3 used, 0.7 battered. Default 0.4. |

## `set_lighting`

Choose the lighting for previews and the viewer: studio (neutral, best for judging), outdoor (sun and sky), sunset (warm, dramatic), night (cool, dim). Check important models under more than one.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` (required) | one of `studio`, `outdoor`, `sunset`, `night` |  |

## `render_preview`

Render the scene and return an image so you can check your work. Use it after every few edits and fix what looks wrong. Default views: front, right, top and three_quarter in a 2x2 grid (left to right, top to bottom).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `focus` | array of integer | Object ids to zoom in on (a close-up of small parts such as a hilt or a handle). The rest of the scene is still drawn. |
| `size` | integer | Pixels per view, 128 to 1024. Default 384. |
| `views` | array of string |  |

## `export_glb`

Save the whole scene as a .glb file (glTF 2.0) for Unity, Unreal, Godot, Blender or the web.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` (required) | string | File path ending in .glb. |

## `save_project`

Save the editable scene (meshes, materials, baked textures, lighting) as a .meshmind project file, so work can continue later with open_project. Save before ending a session.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` (required) | string | File path ending in .meshmind. |

## `open_project`

Replace the current scene with a .meshmind project saved earlier. Can be undone.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` (required) | string | File path ending in .meshmind. |

## `undo`

Undo the last change to the scene.

## `redo`

Redo the last undone change.
